allocation.topic: budget unit (combination wells / orientation measurements) leaves plates, controls and rounds unmatched
allocation.assumption: equal orientation measurements (or equal combination wells) is an equal budget
allocation.evidence: custom plates (branch-separate / joint packing): verify_hits_terminal 1,484 / 1,114.5 (5 rounds); fixed_split_dev 1,293.5 / 1,136.5 (5 rounds) but 663.5 / 506.5 when run in its sufficient 2 rounds; paired_full 1,696 / 1,658.5 (4 rounds) but 507.5 / 492 in its sufficient 1 round; screen_only 927. Combination wells differ by at most 1.8% across these arms (paired lowest, 79,373 vs 80,787 measurement version), yet custom plates fill only 24-37% of their wells because every line needs its own plates in every round and branch. Each custom plate carries at least 200 control wells (screening documentation). The raw Jaaks layout per plate shows 6 NC-0, 114 NC-1, 384 DMSO-tagged, 28 blank, 34 + 34 positive-control and 276 unused positions (repeats/receipts/provenance.json), so the real fixed overhead per plate exceeds 200 wells.
allocation.why_it_matters: if plates, seeding events and controls (not combination wells) dominate cost, verify-hits buys its +9.1% over the 2-round fixed split with about 2.2x the plates (1,484 vs 663.5 branch-separate; 1,114.5 vs 506.5 joint) and 2.5x the calendar time
allocation.what_would_change_the_conclusion: a plate-matched (or seeding-event-matched) replay in which the fixed split and paired arms may spend the plate budget verify-hits consumes; if they then match or beat verify-hits, the advantage is a combination-well accounting artefact of a per-pair custom-plate lab
allocation.request: declare the binding resource before the 2x2 (combination wells, plates, seeding events or days); report all four; never call an arm cheaper on one of them alone

allocation.assumption: a verification-first terminal round R+1 is part of the scheduler, and arms are compared at equal budget irrespective of rounds
allocation.evidence: C6 terminal round vs none +5.9% [3.8, 8.3]; verify-hits needs 5 rounds (20 protocol days), fixed split 2 (8 days), paired 1 (4 days). Post hoc time-matched T1: verify-hits at 2 rounds 210.5 vs fixed split at 2 rounds 231.5 (-9.1% [-14.3, -3.4]); T2: verify-hits at 3 rounds 246.5 vs fixed split at 2 rounds +6.5% [3.0, 10.6]; T3: verify-hits at 2 rounds vs paired at 1 round -1.9% [-8.6, +5.8]
allocation.why_it_matters: the headline +17.7% over paired and +9.1% over the fixed split are trades of rounds (2.5-5x the calendar time) for discoveries, not free gains. 'Static verify-hits is multistage' cuts both ways: the historical 4x-latency argument returns against verify-hits relative to the 1-2 round static designs. Rounds have a measurable value here: 2 -> 3 rounds +17.1% (210.5 -> 246.5), 3 -> 5 rounds +2.4% (246.5 -> 252.5) for verify-hits
allocation.what_would_change_the_conclusion: if the lab's binding constraint is calendar time or seeding events, the 2-round fixed split is the strong baseline and verify-hits loses at equal rounds
allocation.request: the frozen 2x2 must fix the number of rounds R for every arm, select the strong simple baseline at that R (fixed split at R = 2; verify-hits / conf_per_cost at R >= 3), and report the round-response curve (R = 2, 3, 5) instead of a single budget-matched number

allocation.topic: the 2-round verify-hits under-reserves (time-matched comparison is post hoc and partly a reserve-sizing artefact)
allocation.assumption: verify_hits_terminal_R1 is a fair 2-round adaptive scheduler
allocation.evidence: T1 -9.1%: at 2 rounds verify-hits sizes its round-1 reserve from historical screen-call probabilities, while the fixed split reserves f = 0.30-0.40 of the budget (chosen leave-one-tissue-out); T1-T4 were added after the outcome read (plan_addendum_1, D8)
allocation.why_it_matters: a 2-round design is a two-stage design; with an adequately sized reserve, 'verify every hit' and 'fixed split' should nearly coincide, so the T1 gap probably measures reserve calibration rather than adaptivity
allocation.what_would_change_the_conclusion: a 2-round verify-hits whose reserve is set by the same leave-one-tissue-out rule as f; if it matches the fixed split, adaptivity adds nothing at R = 2
allocation.request: label T1-T4 POST HOC and exploratory (done); do not use T1 as evidence against adaptivity until the reserve is matched

allocation.topic: information matching of conf_per_cost (predictor and scheduler confounded)
allocation.assumption: conf_per_cost is a 'simple scheduler' comparable with verify-hits
allocation.evidence: deviation D5 / review note R1: conf_per_cost ranks by other lines' validation-orientation calls (p_sv, p_v_given_s); every other static arm ranks by screen-orientation history. C3: verify-hits minus conf_per_cost -5.8% [-9.3, -2.1] (physical -5.3% [-8.6, -1.7])
allocation.why_it_matters: its lead mixes a validation-aware predictor with a value-per-cost scheduler, so it cannot be attributed to scheduling. Its history also assumes complete both-orientation panels in every history line. A real verify-hits lab observes validation calls only for pairs that were screen hits AND were verified in earlier campaigns (selected, incomplete history), so p_sv is not observable for non-hits
allocation.what_would_change_the_conclusion: (i) restricting conf_per_cost's history to what a verify-hits lab would have observed; (ii) the two off-diagonal cells - validation-aware ranking under the plain verify-hits scheduler, and the value-per-cost scheduler under history_mean ranking. If (ii) puts the gain in the ranking cell, the 'scheduler' contribution is zero
allocation.request: these two cells are exactly the model x scheduler 2x2 on exposed data; run them as exploratory development before any freeze, with history availability declared (complete panel vs verify-hits-observable)

allocation.topic: custom per-pair plates vs native Jaaks plates
allocation.assumption: a pair-orientation can be bought on its own (custom-plate lab)
allocation.evidence: purchased orientations occupy 5.9-10.8% of the combination wells on the native plates they touch (D7). Native plates touched: screen_only 1,111.5, fixed split 1,597.5, verify-hits 1,619.5, paired 1,981.5; a native plate = one line x all about 25 anchors x one library doublet, so one native plate measures about 50 pair-orientations
allocation.why_it_matters: in the native layout the action is a (line, library doublet) plate, the menu per line is 13-26 doublets, and a verification plate co-screens dozens of other pairs. Screening and verification are no longer separable, and the screen/verify trade-off (and the verify-hits advantage) may shrink, vanish or reverse
allocation.what_would_change_the_conclusion: a doublet-granular replay at an equal native-plate budget; if the ranking of schedulers changes, every allocation conclusion is scoped to a hypothetical per-pair dispensing lab
allocation.request: state the scope ('custom per-pair plates, one line per plate') in every claim; add the doublet-granular replay as the next exploratory step or record it as not done

allocation.topic: development selection of the fixed split
allocation.assumption: leave-one-tissue-out f is a fair development-selected comparator
allocation.evidence: chosen f: breast 0.35, colon 0.40, pancreas 0.30; LOTO total 231.5; the in-sample best grid total is 236.5 (f = 0.35 or 0.40); the grid is flat between 0.30 and 0.40 (233.5-236.5)
allocation.why_it_matters: LOTO with 3 heterogeneous tissues could penalise the fixed split. Here it costs at most 5 of the 21-discovery gap, so verify-hits stays +6.8% above even the in-sample-best fixed split. The whole grid is tuned on exposed data (study-level leakage), and a per-line f from the line's own history hit rate (a simple non-adaptive rule) was not tried
allocation.what_would_change_the_conclusion: a per-line history-scaled f closing the remaining gap would make verify-hits' advantage a calibration effect, not an adaptivity effect
allocation.request: report the in-sample best as an upper bound for the fixed split (done as a diagnostic); add a history-scaled split if the 2x2 needs a stronger simple baseline

repeats_preemptive.topic: seeding events as the paper's biological replicates
repeats_preemptive.assumption: seeding event (line, DATE_CREATED) = biological replicate; DAY1 groups = seeding batches
repeats_preemptive.evidence: status CORROBORATED_NOT_AUTHENTICATED: DAY1 groups equal seeding events one-to-one (606 = 606), but 107 fitted plates have no day-1 plate; events per tuple in repeat lines 2-5 (median 4) and plates per event median 1, against the paper's 2-18 (median 4) biological and typically 3 technical
repeats_preemptive.why_it_matters: if the paper's counts mix levels, the inferred hierarchy differs; variance components and any 'independent repeat' claim depend on the level
repeats_preemptive.what_would_change_the_conclusion: if events are not the unit the authors called biological replicates, repeats support 'separate seeding' only

repeats_preemptive.assumption: different seeding events are independent biological repeats
repeats_preemptive.evidence: events per CELL_ID: AU565 18 events from one expansion, HCC1937 15 from one; HCT-15, KP-4, MZ1-PC, PA-TU-8988T, SK-CO-1, SUIT-2, SW620 one CELL_ID each - 9 of 14 lines have every event from one expansion
repeats_preemptive.why_it_matters: seedings from one expansion share passage lineage; between-seeding variance understates between-stock or between-lab variance, so reproducibility and lambda look better than a fresh-stock verification would show
repeats_preemptive.what_would_change_the_conclusion: lower agreement across CELL_IDs in the 5 multi-expansion lines (descriptive only: 5 lines)

repeats_preemptive.assumption: lambda can be estimated with line-level uncertainty
repeats_preemptive.evidence: 14 named lines (5 breast, 4 colon, 5 pancreas); 21,131 tuples with >= 2 events nested in them; 4 further lines (MDA-MB-175-VII, PANC-04-03, PANC-10-05, YAPC) also have a median >= 2 events per doublet but are not paper-documented
repeats_preemptive.why_it_matters: tuple-level resampling would give falsely narrow intervals; with 14 clusters a percentile bootstrap undercovers; the lines were chosen by the authors, not sampled
repeats_preemptive.what_would_change_the_conclusion: a cluster-robust interval (t with 13 df, or a wild cluster bootstrap) that includes lambda = 0
repeats_preemptive.request: declare before outcomes whether the 4 extra lines are included; report n = lines

repeats_preemptive.topic: what lambda measures (self vs transfer) and selection
repeats_preemptive.assumption: prior + lambda x feedback tests whether feedback generalises
repeats_preemptive.evidence: the earlier post hoc found drug-in-line effects transfer across orientations with r 0.16-0.36 and negative out-of-orientation R2
repeats_preemptive.why_it_matters: if 'feedback' is the same pair's own screen residual, lambda is a reliability (regression-to-the-mean) coefficient, positive whenever test-retest reliability > 0. That informs WHICH HITS TO VERIFY, not which new pairs to screen. A cross-pair lambda is the generalisation question. In a verify-hits lab only hits get repeats, so lambda fitted on hits alone is attenuated by truncation
repeats_preemptive.what_would_change_the_conclusion: lambda_self > 0 with lambda_transfer = 0 means the repeat-aware predictor can only improve verification ordering (bounded by the scheduler-only ceiling, about +9.6% at the Jaaks budget), never screening
repeats_preemptive.request: fit and report lambda_self and lambda_transfer separately; fit on all repeated tuples, and also on screen hits only as a lab-realistic sensitivity

repeats_preemptive.topic: repeat verification is not the allocation's verification
repeats_preemptive.assumption: a lambda from same-condition repeats plugs into the role-swapped allocation replay
repeats_preemptive.evidence: repeats = same orientation, same concentrations, different seeding dates months apart (e.g. AU565 2016-03-30 to 2017-06-25); allocation verification = the other orientation in the same campaign
repeats_preemptive.why_it_matters: different estimands and time gaps: months-apart repeats include drift and lot changes that a 4-day in-campaign verification would not
repeats_preemptive.what_would_change_the_conclusion: a declared mapping (or a separate lambda per verification type); without it the 2x2's 'reproducibility-aware predictor' is undefined

repeats_preemptive.evidence: read behind an exposed ticket as plate-level fields
